3\. Core journeys
=================

3.1 Requisition to purchase order
---------------------------------

1.  **Trigger:** IS or PI raises a requisition manually, or the system creates one from a reorder alert or a production shortage (source recorded).
2.  Requisition is submitted; the approval rule engine matches action and amount. Below the limit it goes straight to PI; above it Management is notified.
3.  PI converts the approved requisition to a PO: picks the supplier (item-supplier prices and lead times are suggested), currency, incoterm, mode, expected dates. The system records the exchange rate and shows the estimated duty from HS codes.
4.  PO is submitted; approval by amount (Management). Rejection returns it to PI with the comment.
5.  On approval PI sends the PO (PDF by email); status becomes Sent, then Confirmed when the supplier acknowledges.

**Exceptions:** supplier on hold or blocked stops submission; a PO that pushes a supplier’s period total over the aggregate limit is flagged to Management; edits after approval create a new version and re-trigger approval.

3.2 Import: PO to landed cost
-----------------------------

![Import flow](data:image/png;base64,)  
_Figure 1 — Shipment and landed-cost journey_

1.  PI creates a shipment (mode, BL or AWB, containers, carrier, forwarder, clearing agent, ports, ETD, ETA) and attaches PO lines being shipped; a PO can split across shipments and a shipment can carry several POs.
2.  PI records events as news arrives (departed, transhipped, arrived). If ETA slips by more than the configured days, Management and IS are notified.
3.  On arrival PI opens the customs entry: declaration number, regime, customs value, duty, VAT, levies and status. Uploads required documents; the checklist shows what is missing.
4.  PI enters charges as estimates and replaces them with actuals when agent and carrier invoices arrive; each charge has currency, rate, basis and a recoverable flag.
5.  After release, goods are delivered to the warehouse and IS receives them (journey 3.3).
6.  When charges are final, PI previews and posts the landed-cost run. Lot cost and moving-average cost update; FS sees the accrual and GL postings queue.
7.  Supplier invoice is matched three ways; FS records payments. The shipment closes when documents are complete and charges are actual.

**Exceptions:** customs query or hold sets the shipment to Held with owner and reason; a demurrage clock appears when free days are running out; late charges after posting create a landed-cost adjustment run; a closed period blocks reversal without Management approval.

3.3 Receiving and incoming inspection
-------------------------------------

1.  IS opens the expected receipt from the shipment or PO; the scan field is focused.
2.  For each line IS scans or keys quantity, lot number and component serials (required for CPU, motherboard, SSD, RAM).
3.  Damaged or wrong items are marked rejected with reason and photo and go to the quarantine location.
4.  If the item or supplier requires inspection, a QC Inspector records an incoming inspection (sample size, checklist, defects); a reject moves stock to quarantine.
5.  IS posts the receipt: ledger rows, lots and serials are written; PO and shipment lines update; variance against the PO is shown.
6.  Rejected quantities can open a supplier RMA for PI.

**Exceptions:** over-delivery needs a reason and PI confirmation; a duplicate serial is blocked with a link to the existing record; a partial receipt leaves the PO in Partly received.

3.4 Assembly, tests and quality control
---------------------------------------

![Production flow](data:image/png;base64,)  
_Figure 2 — From assembly order to finished goods_

1.  IS creates an assembly order for stock or for an internal order; the BOM version and routing are snapshotted.
2.  The system checks materials including stock in transit. Shortages create a requisition and hold the order at Awaiting materials; the buildable view shows what limits the model.
3.  IS releases the order: materials are reserved, unit records are created, and IS issues parts to the WIP location by scanning component serials.
4.  The technician (AT) opens a unit, completes checklist steps in order, scans parts as installed and logs time; imaging and licence assignment follow where required.
5.  AT records tests (POST, burn-in, stress, battery, display, network, thermal) with logs.
6.  QI inspects the unit; the system blocks the inspector if they built it. Pass: final serial, cost snapshot, label and finished-goods receipt. Fail: defect codes and a rework order return the unit to the bench; re-inspection is required.
7.  When all units are complete the assembly order closes and yields, labour minutes and defects feed reports.

**Exceptions:** a faulty component found during build is replaced from stock (genealogy updated) and may open a supplier RMA; scrap needs approval above the limit; order on hold keeps reservations until released or cancelled.

3.5 Internal order to dispatch
------------------------------

![Order and dispatch flow](data:image/png;base64,)  
_Figure 3 — Internal sales and dispatch_

1.  IS creates an internal order for a named account (department, staff member, unit) with the source reference (memo, email, LPO), lines and required date. Prices come from the internal price list and are snapshotted when confirmed.
2.  Discounts or price overrides above the limit, or an account above its credit limit, trigger Management approval.
3.  The system checks stock. In-stock lines reserve specific serial units; out-of-stock lines can create an assembly order and show an expected ready date.
4.  When units are ready IS creates the dispatch note, picks, and dispatches. Partial dispatch is allowed.
5.  At handover IS records the recipient name, phone and signature or photo. Warranty starts on this event.
6.  FS issues the invoice or proforma, records payment and allocates it. Cost of sales posts to the ledger from the units’ actual cost.

**Exceptions:** a reserved unit that fails a late check goes back to QC hold and the order is re-reserved; a return is requested, approved by Management, inspected, restocked or quarantined, and credited.

3.6 Warranty claim and repair
-----------------------------

![Service flow](data:image/png;base64,)  
_Figure 4 — After-sales service_

1.  FS logs a claim or repair request by scanning or typing the unit serial. The system shows warranty status, genealogy and component supplier coverage.
2.  A ticket opens with priority and SLA clock; FS assigns an AT.
3.  AT diagnoses and records findings. If covered, parts are issued from stock and genealogy updated. If not covered, FS issues a quote to the account holder; approval is recorded.
4.  Parts are consumed (ledger rows linked to the ticket); AT repairs and retests; QI retests if the repair touched a controlled step.
5.  FS marks Ready for collection and the account contact is emailed; handover is recorded and the ticket closes with true cost (covered repairs post at zero charge).
6.  A faulty component still under supplier warranty opens a supplier RMA for PI.

**Exceptions:** goodwill cover for expired warranty needs Management approval; a loaner unit can be assigned; SLA breach alerts FS and Management.

3.7 Approvals
-------------

![Approval flow](data:image/png;base64,)  
_Figure 5 — Approval handling_

*   Rules are configured by action and amount: PO, stock write-off, discount or price override, refund, expense, supplier bank change, landed-cost reversal after close, period close.
*   The requester cannot approve their own request; if no approver responds within the SLA the request escalates to the delegate named in the rule.
*   Approving executes the action automatically (for example, the PO becomes Approved); rejecting returns it with the comment. Every decision is audited.
*   Management can approve from a phone: the inbox and the detail view are designed for small screens.

3.8 Stock count and adjustment
------------------------------

1.  IS schedules a cycle count (by location, category or ABC class) or a full stock take; expected quantities are frozen from the ledger at the start.
2.  Counters enter quantities by scanning or keying; QI may witness high-value areas.
3.  Variances are listed with value; IS recommends reason codes.
4.  Variances above the limit go for Management approval; on approval an adjustment posts ledger rows and a GL entry.
5.  The count closes; accuracy figures feed the KPI.

3.9 Month-end close
-------------------

1.  FS opens the close checklist: all receipts posted, landed-cost runs final, supplier invoices matched, payments allocated, adjustments approved, bank reconciliation done.
2.  The system flags open items by owner and notifies them.
3.  FS runs the trial balance and exports journals, invoices and payments for UPSA finance.
4.  FS requests the period close; Management approves; the period locks (closed).
5.  Corrections after close post in the current period; reopening needs Management approval and is audited.

3.10 Onboarding and data import
-------------------------------

1.  SA invites a user by email with a role template; the user sets a password and enrols TOTP on first sign-in.
2.  SA can adjust scopes; Management is notified of any scope change.
3.  Data import wizard: choose a template (items, suppliers, accounts, BOMs, opening stock), upload Excel or CSV, review validation (row errors with reasons), commit; a batch can be rolled back until used.
4.  Opening stock is imported as ledger receipts to the correct locations, then verified by a supervised stock count.

4\. State machines
==================

Transitions not listed are rejected by database functions. Each transition records actor and time in the event timeline and audit log.

### Purchase order

| **From** | **To** | **Who** | **Condition** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| draft | pending\_approval | PI | Lines, supplier, currency, rate complete |
| pending\_approval | approved / draft | MG | Approve, or reject with comment |
| approved | sent | PI | Email sent |
| sent | confirmed | PI | Supplier acknowledgement recorded |
| confirmed | partly\_received / received | IS (via receipt) | Derived from posted receipts |
| received | closed | PI | Invoices matched |
| any open | cancelled | PI | No posted receipts; approval if above limit |

### Shipment

| **From** | **To** | **Who** | **Condition** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| booked | in\_transit | PI | Departure event |
| in\_transit | arrived | PI | Arrival date recorded |
| arrived | customs\_processing | PI | Customs entry lodged |
| customs\_processing | held | PI | Query or inspection hold with reason |
| customs\_processing / held | cleared | PI | Duty paid; release recorded |
| cleared | delivered | IS / PI | Goods at warehouse |
| delivered | closed | PI | Receipt posted; documents complete; charges actual; landed cost posted |

### Requisition, internal order, assembly order

| **Object** | **Path** |
| --- | --- |
| Requisition | draft → submitted → approved → converted · or rejected · or cancelled |
| Internal order | draft → pending\_approval → approved → awaiting\_build (optional) → ready → dispatched → completed · or cancelled |
| Assembly order | draft → planned → awaiting\_materials ⇄ ready → released → in\_progress → in\_qc → completed · on\_hold and cancelled from any open state |

### Ticket, RMA, invoice, count

| **Object** | **Path** |
| --- | --- |
| Service ticket | received → diagnosing → (awaiting\_approval) → (awaiting\_parts) → in\_repair → testing → ready\_for\_collection → closed · or declined |
| Supplier RMA | draft → submitted → authorised → shipped → credited or replaced → closed · or rejected |
| Invoice | draft → issued → part\_paid → paid · overdue is derived · void with credit note |
| Stock count | planned → counting → review → posted · or cancelled |
| Fiscal period | open → soft\_closed → closed (reopen needs approval) |

5\. Notification matrix
=======================

In-app and email only. Each user can switch email off per category except approvals and security.

| **Event** | **Recipients** | **Channel** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Approval requested / decided / escalated | Approver; requester | In-app + email |
| Shipment ETA slips, held, arrived, released | PI, IS, MG | In-app + email |
| Demurrage free days ≤ 3 | PI, MG | In-app + email |
| Goods receipt posted with variance | PI, FS | In-app |
| Low stock or reorder suggestion | IS, PI | In-app + daily email digest |
| Landed-cost run posted | FS, MG | In-app |
| Assembly order blocked by materials | IS, PI | In-app |
| Unit ready for QC / rework returned | QI / AT | In-app |
| Order ready for dispatch; dispatched | IS; account contact (email) | In-app; email |
| Invoice issued; payment overdue | Account contact; FS | Email; in-app |
| Ticket assigned; SLA at risk or breached | AT; FS, MG | In-app + email |
| Warranty expiring in 30 days | FS | In-app |
| Scope change, new user, suspended user | MG | Email |
| Scheduled report ready | Requester | Email with signed link |
| Failed job or posting | SA | In-app + email |

6\. Edge cases and error flows
==============================

| **Situation** | **Behaviour** |
| --- | --- |
| Two users edit the same document | Second save returns 412 with the latest version and a field-level diff to merge |
| Scan not found | Clear message with options: search manually, create item (if permitted), or report |
| Serial entered twice | Blocked; shows where the serial already lives |
| Receipt posted twice (double click or retry) | Idempotency key returns the first result; no duplicate ledger rows |
| Exchange rate missing for a date | Document cannot post; prompt to add a rate with source or choose the nearest approved rate |
| Closed period | Postings go to the current period with a banner; reversals need approval |
| Landed-cost charge arrives late | Adjustment run: remaining stock adjusts the average; consumed portion posts to variance |
| Landed-cost allocation would exceed the charge by rounding | Largest-remainder method guarantees equality |
| Reserved unit fails inspection | Reservation released, order flagged, IS offered substitutes |
| Approver unavailable | Escalates to delegate after the SLA; Management sees overdue approvals |
| Insufficient stock for issue | Issue blocked; shortage shown with in-transit quantities and a create-requisition shortcut |
| Supplier bank detail changed | Payments to that supplier are blocked until the change is verified and approved |
| Large export | Runs as a background job; user is notified and receives a signed link |
| Browser offline or connection lost | Unsaved form data is kept locally; a banner explains; nothing is posted until the server confirms |
| Session expiry or MFA failure | Redirect to sign-in preserving the target; repeated failures lock the account and alert SA |
| User without scope opens a link | 403 page naming the missing capability and how to request it |

7\. A working day by role
=========================

| **Role** | **Typical day** |
| --- | --- |
| SA | Review failed jobs and security alerts; handle invitations and leavers; check backups and audit exceptions weekly |
| MG | Clear the approvals inbox; scan the home screen for delayed shipments, shortages and budget variance; review weekly KPIs and exceptions |
| PI | Chase shipments; update events and customs status; enter charges as invoices arrive; raise POs from approved requisitions; post landed-cost runs |
| IS | Receive goods; release and issue assembly orders; process internal orders and dispatches; run cycle counts; handle low-stock alerts |
| FS | Issue invoices; allocate payments; review service tickets and SLA; record expenses; prepare month-end |
| AT | Pick up the next unit from the queue; complete steps and tests; handle repairs assigned to them |
| QI | Inspect incoming goods and finished units; log defects; retest reworked units |

8\. Screen states and interaction rules
=======================================

*   **Loading:** skeleton rows for lists, spinner only inside buttons; blocking operations over one second show progress.
*   **Empty:** each empty state explains why it is empty and offers the next action permitted for the role.
*   **Error:** inline message with remedy and trace id; retry where safe.
*   **Saving documents:** drafts autosave; posting actions need explicit confirmation showing what will be written (ledger rows, cost change, notifications).
*   **Destructive actions:** void, cancel and reverse need a reason; irreversible ones need a second confirmation.
*   **Search:** global search accepts serials, document numbers, supplier names and BL/AWB numbers; results grouped by type and filtered by the user’s scopes.
*   **Keyboard:** Ctrl/Cmd+K command palette, / filter, G then letter to jump to a module, Esc closes drawers.
*   **Audit trail:** every document has a timeline tab showing events and audit entries to users with the scope.
